Consider all circular sectors $JKL$ with area $A=121$ square units. Determine the radius $r$ of the circular sector with the smallest possible perimeter. Do not round the answer.

$r=$
{{field-1}}
units
question.worked_solution:
We let $r$ be the radius of the circular sector and let $\theta $ be the angle (in radians) subtended by it. Then, we want to minimize the perimeter

$$
P=2r+r\theta .
$$

We know that the area is fixed at $121$ square units, so we also have the constraint condition

$$
121=\frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}\theta .
$$

Now, by making $\theta $ the subject of the constraint equation and taking into account that $r>0,$ we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}121 & =\frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}\theta  \\ \theta  & =\frac{242}{{r}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging this into our expression for $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =2r+r\theta  \\  & =2r+r\cdot \frac{242}{{r}^{2}} \\  & =2r+\frac{242}{r}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $P,$ so we need to differentiate $P$ and set the derivative equal to zero. Computing the derivative gives

$$
{P}^{′}(r)=2-\frac{242}{{r}^{2}}.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2-\frac{242}{{r}^{2}} & =0 \\ 2{r}^{2} & =242 \\ {r}^{2} & =121 \\ r & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we confirm that $r=11$ is a minimum using the second derivative test.

Since the second derivative ${P}^{″}(r)=\frac{484}{{r}^{3}}>0,$ the stationary point $r=11$ is a minimum.

Therefore, the radius of the circular sector with the smallest perimeter is $r=11$ units.
